description_full: KLA Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, provides process control and process-enabling solutions for manufacturing wafers, reticles/masks, chemicals/materials, integrated circuits (ICs), packaged ICs, and printed circuit boards. It operates through three segments: Semiconductor Process Control; Specialty Semiconductor Process; and PCB and Component Inspection. The company offers inspection and review tools to identify, locate, characterize, review, and analyze defects on various surfaces of patterned and unpatterned wafers; chemical process control equipment; wired and wireless sensor wafers and reticles; wafer defect inspection, review, and metrology systems; reticle inspection and metrology systems; wafer inspection and metrology systems; semiconductor software solutions; KLA Pro systems; and specialty semiconductor manufacturing, benchtop metrology, surface characterization, material strength characterization, and electrical property measurement products. It also provides etch, plasma dicing, deposition and other wafer processing technologies and solutions; direct imaging, inspection, optical shaping, inkjet, and additive printing, as well as computer-aided manufacturing and engineering solutions; and components. In addition, the company offers service programs. It serves semiconductor, and semiconductor-related and electronic device manufacturers. The company operates in China, Taiwan, Korea, North America, Japan, Europe, Israel, and rest of Asia. The company was formerly known as KLA-Tencor Corporation and changed its name to KLA Corporation in July 2019. KLA Corporation was incorporated in 1975 and is headquartered in Milpitas, California.

financial_summary: KLA Corporation is a large-cap technology business with a $183.5B market cap on $13.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years and +16% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 55% against a 12% cost of capital — a 43-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $3.8B in free cash flow — roughly 28 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.86× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 21× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.7%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 43% operating margin runs 37pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 536 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 31% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 23% over the last three months.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 54% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 67% and a beta of 1.54, it amplifies market moves.
Liquidity is deep, with about $1.8B traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 37% in the 2020 crash, 40% in the 2022 bear market and 67% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $69.86 (margin of safety -102%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 17%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $23.33 to $193 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: EV/EBITDA 28.1 vs 16.6 and P/FCF 48.7 vs 24.5 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 91% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.1% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 26 covering analysts target $218 on average, 55% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 55% clears the cost of capital of 11.7% by 43pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.38).
It converts 28% of revenue into free cash flow.
ROE of 76% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.8x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 7pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 11.3% of revenue on R&D and 2.3% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.7x net debt to EBITDA ($1.6B of cash against $5.9B of debt), with interest covered 20.7x.
Working capital ties up about 288 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.0% over 3 years, 14.4% over 5 years and 16.4% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 12%).
At current returns, reinvesting 28% of profits supports about 15.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 14.0% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 0.84 (orders lagging sales), a backlog worth 65% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 409%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.0x, 2.8% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 40, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.1%), and institutions hold 92%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (9 sales, net $70.9M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.7% (1.2% in buybacks and 0.7% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 3.1% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 20 consecutive years, raising it 13.6% a year over the last five.
people: With about 17,000 employees, each generates about $799K of revenue, 2.1x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 10.2% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $222K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $6.5M (8x revenue per employee).
